source_text: καὶ ὁ κατηχούμενος ἔτι, καὶ τοῖς τελείοις συναναθεὶς τὴν αἴνεσιν, τῶν ἔτι μυστικωτέρων ἀποφοιτᾷ, καὶ θυσίας εἴργεται τῆς ἐπὶ Χριστῷ. Ταύτῃτοι καλῶς ὁ νόμος προανεφώνει τὴν οἰκονομίαν, καὶ τῆς αἰνέσεως τὴν θυσίαν, ἐπ' ἄρτοις ζυμίταις, καὶ ἐν ἀζύμοις λαγάνοις ποιεῖσθαι προστέταχεν. Ἑκάστου, καθάπερ ἐγᾦμαι, τῶν ὠνομασμένων, ζωῆς εἶδος ὑποσημαίνοντος· ἄρτος μὲν γὰρ ὁ ἐζυμωμένος, βίου καὶ ζωῆς ἔσται τύπος, τῆς οὔπω κεκαθαρμένης διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου βαπτίσματος, οὔτε μὴν εἰσάπαν ἀπηλλαγμένης κοσμικῆς ἀκαθαρσίας· λάγανον δὲ ἄζυμον, τῆς ἤδη διεσμηγμένης ἐν Χριστῷ διὰ πίστεως, τῆς τῶν τελείων, φημὶ, οἷς καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος προσεφώνει, λέγων· «Ὥστε ἑορτάζωμεν, μὴ ἐν ζύμῃ παλαιᾷ, μηδὲ ἐν ζύμῃ κακίας καὶ πονηρίας, ἀλλ' ἐν ἀζύμοις εἰλικρινείας καὶ ἀληθείας.» Καὶ πάλιν· «Ἐκκαθάρατε οὖν τὴν παλαιὰν ζύμην, ἵνα ἦτε νέον φύραμα, καθώς ἐστε ἄζυμοι.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἄριστα ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Σεμίδαλις δὲ πρὸς τούτοις οὔπω πρὸς ἑνότητα συνενηνεγμένη, καθὰ καὶ ἐν ἄρτῳ καὶ ἐν λαγάνῳ τυχὸν, μένουσα δὲ ὥσπερ ἐν κόκκοις ἔτι, τὸ ὡς ἓν καθ' ἕκαστον καὶ καθ' ἕνα τῶν προσκομιζόντων τὴν αἴνεσιν ὑπαινίττεται· δεκτοὶ γάρ ἐσμεν τῷ Θεῷ, ποιούμενοι τὰς δοξολογίας, καὶ ἀνὰ μέρος ἕκαστος, καὶ ὡς ἓν οἱ πάντες κατὰ πληθύν. Ἐπιχεῖται δὲ τὸ ἔλαιον τῇ τῆς αἰνέσεως θυσίᾳ, τὸ ἱλαρὸν τοῦ πράγματος ὑποσημαῖνον, καὶ ὅτι πάντη τε καὶ πάντως ἕψεται παρὰ Θεῷ τὸ ἐλεεῖσθαι δεῖν τοῖς προσάγειν εἰωθόσιν αὐτήν. «Θῦσον γὰρ, φησὶ, τῷ Θεῷ θυσίαν αἰνέσεως, καὶ ἀπόδος τῷ Ὑψίστῳ τὰς εὐχάς σου· καὶ ἐπικάλεσαί με ἐν ἡμέρᾳ θλίψεώς σου, καὶ ἐξελοῦμαί σε, καὶ δοξάσεις με.» Γράφει δέ που καὶ ὁ Χριστοῦ μαθητής· «Ἀθυμεῖ τις ἐν ὑμῖν; προσευχέσθω· εὐθυμεῖ; ψαλλέτω.» Οὐκοῦν ἐν ἄρτοις ἐζυμωμένοις, καὶ ἐν ἀζύμοις λαγάνοις, καὶ ἐν κεγχρεμίσιν ἔτι σεμιδάλεως ἐκπράττεσθαι δεῖν τῆς αἰνέσεως τὴν θυσίαν, διετύπου σαφῶς· ἑνὸς δὲ ἀφ' ἑκάστου προσαγομένου, καὶ ὡς ἐν δρακὶ μιᾷ τῆς σεμιδάλεως, σφαζομένου τε προβάτου, καὶ τῶν ἐντοσθίων θυομένων κατὰ τὸν νόμον, ἐδώδιμα τὰ λοιπὰ τοῖς ἱερουργεῖν ἐπιτεταγμένοις, οὐκ ἀκερδῆ τὴν ἱερωσύνην καταδεικνύντος τοῦ νόμου· προσεπιτάττει λέγων· «Ἐν ᾗ ἡμέρᾳ δωρεῖται, βρωθήσεται· οὐ καταλείψουσιν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ πρωΐ.» Δι' οὗ δὴ πάλιν ἔπεισι νοεῖν ἐκεῖνό που τάχα· παρελάσαντος γὰρ τοῦ καιροῦ, καὶ παρῳχηκότος τοῦ αἰῶνος τοῦ ἐνεστηκότος καθάπερ ἡμέρας, δοξολογίας ἡμῖν ἐπινοηθήσεται παρ' οὓς ἴσμεν τρόπος ἕτερος. Ὥσπερ γὰρ τῆς ἐπὶ τῷ Φαραὼ δυναστείας ἐλευθερωθέντες ἡδόμενοι ἐν νόμῳ ἔλεγον, «Ἄσωμεν τῷ Κυρίῳ· ἐνδόξως γὰρ δεδόξασται· ἵππον καὶ ἀναβάτην ἔῤῥιψεν εἰς θάλασσαν.» Λαμπρότερα δὲ ἀσυγκρίτως καὶ ὑπερκείμενα προαναθεωροῦντες ἐν πνεύματι τῆς τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν ἐπιδημίας τὰ κατορθώματα, διακεκράγασι τῶν ἁγίων τινές· «Ἄσατε τῷ Κυρίῳ ᾆσμα καινόν·» τοῦτο δὲ ἦν, «Ἀνέβη ὁ Θεὸς ἐν ἀλαλαγμῷ,» σκυλεύσας τὸν ᾅδην, «καὶ εἰπὼν
pass_a_gloss: [there joins in bringing up the offering] also the one still being catechized, and having offered up the praise together with the perfect, he goes away from the still more mystical things and is barred from the sacrifice in Christ. Therefore the law rightly proclaimed beforehand the arrangement, and commanded the sacrifice of praise to be made upon leavened loaves and in unleavened wafers. Each of the things named, as I think, hints at a form of life; for the leavened bread will be a type of a way of life and a life not yet cleansed through holy baptism, nor indeed wholly freed from worldly uncleanness; and the unleavened wafer, of the one already wiped clean in Christ through faith, of the perfect, I mean, to whom the inspired Paul also called out, saying: 'So let us keep the feast, not in old leaven, nor in leaven of malice and wickedness, but in unleavened things of sincerity and truth.' And again: 'Cleanse out then the old leaven, that you may be a new lump, as you are unleavened.' PALL.: You spoke excellently. CYR.: And the fine flour besides these, not yet brought together into unity, as perhaps in a loaf and in a wafer, but remaining as it were still in grains, hints at the as-one in each and for each one of those bringing the praise; for we are acceptable to God, making the doxologies both each in part and all as one in multitude. And the oil is poured on the sacrifice of praise, hinting at the cheerfulness of the thing, and that in every way and by all means being pitied will follow from God for those accustomed to bring it. 'For sacrifice to God,' he says, 'a sacrifice of praise, and pay your vows to the Most High; and call upon me in the day of your affliction, and I will deliver you, and you will glorify me.' And the disciple of Christ also writes somewhere: 'Is anyone among you downcast? Let him pray; is he cheerful? Let him sing psalms.' So he clearly outlined that the sacrifice of praise must be carried out in leavened loaves, and in unleavened wafers, and still in grains of fine flour; and one being brought from each, and as in a single handful of the fine flour, and a sheep being slaughtered, and the inward parts sacrificed according to the law, the rest are eatable for those appointed to minister, the law showing that the priesthood is not without gain; he adds the command, saying: 'On the day on which it is given it shall be eaten; they shall not leave any of it until morning.' Through which again it occurs to understand that perhaps; for when the time has driven past, and the present age has gone by like a day, another manner of doxology beyond those we know will be devised for us. For as those freed from the tyranny of Pharaoh, rejoicing, said under the law: 'Let us sing to the Lord; for gloriously has he been glorified; horse and rider he has thrown into the sea.' And some of the saints, seeing beforehand in the Spirit the incomparably brighter and surpassing achievements of the sojourn of our Saviour, cried aloud: 'Sing to the Lord a new song'; and this was: 'God went up with a shout,' having despoiled Hades, 'and saying
pass_b_english: Cyril: …the catechumen too, who is still under instruction; and after he has offered the praise together with the perfect, he withdraws from the more sacred mysteries and is kept from the sacrifice that is in Christ. This is why the law did well to foretell this arrangement, when it commanded that the sacrifice of praise be made with leavened loaves and with unleavened wafers (Leviticus 7:12–13). Each of the things named, I think, points to a kind of life. The leavened bread will be a type of a life not yet cleansed through holy baptism, nor yet wholly freed from the world’s uncleanness. The unleavened wafer is a type of the life already washed clean in Christ through faith: the life of the perfect, I mean, whom the inspired Paul also addressed when he said: ‘Let us therefore keep the feast, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth’ (1 Corinthians 5:8). And again: ‘So cleanse out the old leaven, that you may be a new lump, as you are unleavened’ (1 Corinthians 5:7).

Cyril: Besides these, the fine flour, not yet brought together into one mass as it is in a loaf or a wafer, but still remaining, as it were, in its grains, hints that each of those who offer the praise does so as one by himself. For we are acceptable to God when we give him glory both each of us on our own and all of us together as one company. Oil is poured on the sacrifice of praise, signifying the gladness of the act, and that mercy from God will in every way and without fail follow those who are accustomed to offer it. For it says: ‘Offer to God a sacrifice of praise, and pay your vows to the Most High; and call upon me in the day of your affliction, and I will deliver you, and you shall glorify me’ (Psalm 50:14–15). And the disciple of Christ also writes: ‘Is anyone among you downcast? Let him pray. Is anyone cheerful? Let him sing praise’ (James 5:13). So the law clearly showed in figure that the sacrifice of praise must be carried out with leavened loaves, with unleavened wafers, and with fine flour still in its grains. One portion of each was brought forward (Leviticus 7:14), and of the fine flour, as it were, a single handful; a sheep was slaughtered and its inner parts were burnt according to the law; and the rest was food for those appointed to serve as priests, the law thus showing that the priesthood does not go unrewarded. And it adds a further command: ‘On the day it is offered it shall be eaten; they shall not leave any of it until the morning’ (Leviticus 7:15). Through this, again, we may perhaps understand something like this: when the time has run its course, and the present age has passed like a day, another manner of giving glory, beyond those we know, will be devised for us. For just as those under the law, when they had been set free from Pharaoh’s tyranny, said with joy: ‘Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been greatly glorified; horse and rider he has thrown into the sea’ (Exodus 15:1); and just as some of the saints, foreseeing in the Spirit the achievements of our Savior’s coming, which are incomparably brighter and greater, cried aloud: ‘Sing to the Lord a new song’ (Psalm 98:1), and this was: ‘God has gone up with a shout’ (Psalm 47:5), when he had despoiled Hades, ‘and said

choices.why: Leviticus 7:12–13 LXX supplies the terms: θυσία αἰνέσεως (the thank offering, here 'sacrifice of praise'), λάγανα ἄζυμα (7:12), σεμίδαλις (7:12), ἄρτοι ζυμῖται (7:13); κεγχρεμίς is 'grain' (of flour).
ἐν νόμῳ with ἔλεγον rendered 'those under the law' (the people in the time of the law).
ἐν πνεύματι rendered 'in the Spirit' (prophetic sight).
Exodus 15:1 LXX ἐνδόξως δεδόξασται rendered 'He has been greatly glorified' (not the calque 'gloriously glorified').

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 12 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Section opens mid-sentence: ὁ κατηχούμενος is the subject of συναναφέρει at the end of section 27 ('together with those already cleansed through holy baptism … offers the sacrifice'), so the English begins with the catechumen joining in. Leviticus 7:12–13 LXX supplies the terms: θυσία αἰνέσεως (the thank offering, here 'sacrifice of praise'), λάγανα ἄζυμα (7:12), σεμίδαλις (7:12), ἄρτοι ζυμῖται (7:13); κεγχρεμίς is 'grain' (of flour). Cyril quotes 1 Corinthians 5:8 before 5:7; kept in his order. The oil (ἔλαιον) and mercy (ἐλεεῖσθαι) pairing is a sound play in Greek that English cannot keep. Psalm 50:14–15 = LXX Psalm 49:14–15. James 5:13: Cyril reads Ἀθυμεῖ ('downcast') where the New Testament text has Κακοπαθεῖ ('suffering'); translated as he reads. 'One portion of each' = Leviticus 7:14 (ἓν ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν δώρων). 'A single handful' (ὡς ἐν δρακὶ μιᾷ) recalls the grain-offering handful of Leviticus 2:2, but the link to the thank offering is loose, so it is left uncited; the slaughtered sheep and burnt entrails summarise the peace-offering rite of Leviticus 3, also left uncited. ἐν νόμῳ with ἔλεγον rendered 'those under the law' (the people in the time of the law). 'Sing to the Lord a new song' is word for word in LXX Psalms 95:1, 97:1 and 149:1 (English 96:1, 98:1, 149:1); cited as Psalm 98:1 (LXX 97:1) because its next words ('for He has done marvelous things … His right hand has saved') match Cyril's 'achievements', but Psalm 96:1 is equally possible. Psalm 47:5 = LXX Psalm 46:6. 'When He had despoiled Hades' (σκυλεύσας τὸν ᾅδην) is Cyril's own gloss between two quotations, so it stands outside the quotation marks. ἐν πνεύματι rendered 'in the Spirit' (prophetic sight). The sentence runs on into section 29 with Isaiah 49:9; the closing 'in the same way' comes there. Exodus 15:1 LXX ἐνδόξως δεδόξασται rendered 'He has been greatly glorified' (not the calque 'gloriously glorified'). εἰπών closing the sentence is rendered 'and said' so it runs on from 'when He had despoiled Hades'.

Drafted Pass A, kept as written (rewritten as a literal English gloss from the Greek in pass_a_gloss): [cont. from 27: ὁμοῦ τοῖς κεκαθαρμένοις διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου βαπτίσματος συναναφέρει τὸ θῦμα] καὶ ὁ κατηχούμενος ἔτι 'also the one still catechised' (subject of συναναφέρει), καὶ τοῖς τελείοις συναναθεὶς τὴν αἴνεσιν 'having offered up the praise with the perfect', τῶν ἔτι μυστικωτέρων ἀποφοιτᾷ 'departs from the still more mystical (rites)', θυσίας εἴργεται τῆς ἐπὶ Χριστῷ 'is shut out from the sacrifice in Christ'. Ταύτῃτοι καλῶς ὁ νόμος προανεφώνει τὴν οἰκονομίαν 'therefore the law rightly proclaimed beforehand the arrangement', and προστέταχεν 'commanded' the θυσία αἰνέσεως 'sacrifice of praise' to be made ἐπ' ἄρτοις ζυμίταις 'on leavened loaves' καὶ ἐν ἀζύμοις λαγάνοις 'and in unleavened wafers'. Each named thing ζωῆς εἶδος ὑποσημαίνοντος 'hinting a kind of life': ἄρτος ἐζυμωμένος = τύπος βίου καὶ ζωῆς τῆς οὔπω κεκαθαρμένης διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου βαπτίσματος 'not yet cleansed through holy baptism', οὔτε εἰσάπαν ἀπηλλαγμένης κοσμικῆς ἀκαθαρσίας 'nor wholly freed from worldly uncleanness'; λάγανον ἄζυμον = τῆς ἤδη διεσμηγμένης ἐν Χριστῷ διὰ πίστεως 'already washed off in Christ through faith', τῆς τῶν τελείων 'of the perfect', whom ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος addressed: 1 Cor 5:8 ἑορτάζωμεν μὴ ἐν ζύμῃ παλαιᾷ... ἀλλ' ἐν ἀζύμοις εἰλικρινείας καὶ ἀληθείας; again 1 Cor 5:7 ἐκκαθάρατε τὴν παλαιὰν ζύμην ἵνα ἦτε νέον φύραμα καθώς ἐστε ἄζυμοι. PALL. Ἄριστα ἔφης 'best you spoke'. CYR. Σεμίδαλις 'fine flour' οὔπω πρὸς ἑνότητα συνενηνεγμένη 'not yet brought into unity' (as in loaf/wafer), μένουσα ὥσπερ ἐν κόκκοις 'remaining as in grains', ὑπαινίττεται 'hints' τὸ ὡς ἓν καθ' ἕκαστον καὶ καθ' ἕνα 'the as-one each and singly' of those offering praise; δεκτοὶ τῷ Θεῷ 'acceptable to God' giving δοξολογίας both ἀνὰ μέρος ἕκαστος 'each in turn' and ὡς ἓν οἱ πάντες κατὰ πληθύν 'all as one in a multitude'. Ἐπιχεῖται τὸ ἔλαιον 'the oil is poured on', ὑποσημαῖνον τὸ ἱλαρόν 'signifying the cheerfulness', and that πάντη τε καὶ πάντως ἕψεται παρὰ Θεῷ τὸ ἐλεεῖσθαι 'in every way and wholly being shown mercy from God will follow' those offering it. Ps 49:14–15 LXX Θῦσον τῷ Θεῷ θυσίαν αἰνέσεως... ἐπικάλεσαί με ἐν ἡμέρᾳ θλίψεώς σου, καὶ ἐξελοῦμαί σε, καὶ δοξάσεις με. ὁ Χριστοῦ μαθητής: Ἀθυμεῖ τις; προσευχέσθω· εὐθυμεῖ; ψαλλέτω. Οὐκοῦν... διετύπου σαφῶς 'so it clearly figured' the sacrifice in leavened loaves, unleavened wafers, ἐν κεγχρεμίσιν σεμιδάλεως 'in grains of fine flour'; gen. abs.: ἑνὸς ἀφ' ἑκάστου προσαγομένου 'one from each being brought', ὡς ἐν δρακὶ μιᾷ 'as in one handful' of flour, σφαζομένου προβάτου 'a sheep slaughtered', τῶν ἐντοσθίων θυομένων 'the entrails burnt' κατὰ τὸν νόμον, ἐδώδιμα τὰ λοιπά 'the rest edible' for τοῖς ἱερουργεῖν ἐπιτεταγμένοις 'those appointed to officiate', οὐκ ἀκερδῆ τὴν ἱερωσύνην καταδεικνύντος 'showing the priesthood not without gain'. προσεπιτάττει: Lev 7:15 Ἐν ᾗ ἡμέρᾳ δωρεῖται, βρωθήσεται· οὐ καταλείψουσιν εἰς τὸ πρωΐ. Δι' οὗ ἔπεισι νοεῖν 'through which it comes to mind to understand': παρελάσαντος τοῦ καιροῦ 'the time having driven past', παρῳχηκότος τοῦ αἰῶνος τοῦ ἐνεστηκότος καθάπερ ἡμέρας 'the present age gone by like a day', δοξολογίας ἐπινοηθήσεται παρ' οὓς ἴσμεν τρόπος ἕτερος 'another manner of doxology beyond those we know will be devised'. Ὥσπερ γάρ 'for just as' those freed τῆς ἐπὶ τῷ Φαραὼ δυναστείας 'from the dominion under Pharaoh', ἡδόμενοι ἐν νόμῳ ἔλεγον 'rejoicing said in (the time of) the law' Ex 15:1 Ἄσωμεν τῷ Κυρίῳ... ἵππον καὶ ἀναβάτην ἔῤῥιψεν εἰς θάλασσαν; Λαμπρότερα ἀσυγκρίτως καὶ ὑπερκείμενα 'incomparably brighter and surpassing' προαναθεωροῦντες ἐν πνεύματι 'beholding beforehand in spirit' τὰ κατορθώματα 'the achievements' τῆς τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἐπιδημίας 'of the Saviour's sojourn/coming', διακεκράγασι τῶν ἁγίων τινές 'some of the saints cried out' Ἄσατε τῷ Κυρίῳ ᾆσμα καινόν; τοῦτο δὲ ἦν 'and this was' Ἀνέβη ὁ Θεὸς ἐν ἀλαλαγμῷ, σκυλεύσας τὸν ᾅδην 'having despoiled Hades', καὶ εἰπών 'and having said' [cont. 29].

changes: κατὰ πληθύν: 'in the congregation' (added sense) -> 'as one company'
εἰπών: 'and saying' -> 'and said' to run on with 'when He had despoiled Hades'
